scope: Add a fail-closed AC1021+ DXF TABLESTYLE emitter for a small typed DWG-origin profile, preserving the existing raw TABLESTYLE replay path for DXF-origin data.

supportedProfile.source: typed dx_data marked DWG-origin; this slice does not execute a DWG parser
supportedProfile.textStyle: each source handle resolves to exactly one emitted STYLE name
supportedProfile.colors: indexed values 0 through 255 only; ambiguous 256/truecolor/by-layer values are rejected
supportedProfile.borders: six conventional slots with identical lineweight, visibility, and indexed color; no double-line spacing or unsupported border metadata
supportedProfile.formatPayload: custom cell styles, non-default row data/unit/format fields, unknown handles, and unsupported values are rejected

changes: Added dxfRW::writeTableStyle with bounded profile validation, handle/owner emission, and documented TABLESTYLE tags for the core record and three repeated row-style groups.
The adapter emits exactly one typed TABLESTYLE for a DWG-origin graph; DXF-origin TABLESTYLE records continue through exact raw replay.
The extension graph and ACAD_TABLE preflight now admit a typed-only TABLESTYLE graph only for DWG-origin data, retaining raw/typed identity pairing for DXF-origin data.
Generated ASCII and binary tests verify literal group values, reminted style and owner identity, parseback, and fail-closed rejection that preserves an existing destination.

evidence.use: Primary DXF group-code reference for TABLESTYLE identity, owner/subclass, margins, suppression flags, row text settings, indexed colors, and six border-code families.
evidence.limit: The documentation does not fully define row-role ordering or all newer/custom style fields; this emitter preserves the typed row sequence and rejects unmodeled format/custom payloads.

evidence.use: Primary DXF reference for TABLE group 342 style reference and related versioned table style fields.
evidence.limit: Does not establish that the local DWG parser produces a fully equivalent TABLESTYLE model or that an application renders this output identically.
